basis: Mitochondrial myopathy defines ophthalmoplegia; parkinsonism in 2/2 and sensory neuropathy in 1/2 support neurologic involvement, though samples are small.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; endocrine failure is a separately diagnosed complication.
Isolated unilateral shortening of toe bones.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure and dysphagia reflect muscle weakness. Pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiomyopathy occur in 5-29%.
Localized benign necrotic and fibrotic hepatic lesion; the liver is not an endocrine gland for this classification.
Developmental delay is the principal functional phenotype; cardiac, dental and ocular anomalies vary, without evidence that damaging lesions affect at least 30%.
Mitochondrial complex I defect with developmental delay in 2/2; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular involvement. Neurogenic bladder reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Gonococcal infection of the endometrium; the reproductive location has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism does.
Systemic bacterial infection; arthralgia and myalgia alone do not establish tissue damage. Destructive osteoarticular involvement is not established at 30% for this subtype.
Myopathy, weakness and joint abnormalities define the disorder; atrophic scars in 3/5 support common skin damage. Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Mitochondrial myopathy causes progressive extraocular muscle weakness and ptosis; additional neurologic and systemic damage varies across subtypes.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in the jejunum; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability and brain malformations; impaired retinal electrophysiology in 1/1 supports ocular dysfunction, with limited sampling.
Isolated congenital nail absence and dystrophy.
Oxidative phosphorylation defect with lactic acidosis, cardiomyopathy and developmental encephalopathy; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Effusions do not establish direct lung damage.
Inherited myxomatous mitral valve disease causing prolapse and regurgitation.
Isolated absence of mammary glands; breast has no axis.
Inflammatory disease of cervical lymph nodes; no evidence of blood-cell disease or another affected organ.
Alzheimer neurodegeneration with dementia and cerebral cortical atrophy.
Fractures, joint hypermobility and skin fragility define the overlap syndrome. Blue sclerae do not impair vision; arterial rupture occurs in 1/5.
Spastic paraplegia within P5CS deficiency; cataracts are a defining feature of the classical SPG9 phenotype, although frequency varies across this umbrella.
Microphthalmia with ocular cysts and limb malformations define the syndrome; facial clefts alone do not establish oral or airway involvement.
Benign adenoma of the rete ovarii, a reproductive structure; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Renal cysts and encephalocele 11/11; hepatic fibrosis 7/7; pulmonary hypoplasia 6/6. Polydactyly, clubfeet and oral clefts omitted under the cap, prioritizing severe organ defects.
